# Verify speed study 2026-10-15 (d3-mini hosted; 547 claims; metrics = baseline cross-fitted bars)

variant | recall@1%FS | recall@2%FS | true/false@0.99 | judg | req | chars | wall | s/j | OK
baseline 512 exh | 93.3 | 98.1 | 198/0 | 36506 | 36506 | 85M est | 3179s | .087 | -
chunk1024 exh | 93.3 | 98.5 | 214/0 | 20955 | 20979 | 57.2M | 961s | .046 | yes
chunk2048 exh | 96.7 | 98.9 | 225/0 | 12459 | 12459 | 52.6M | 643s | .052 | yes
topk3 | 88.8 | 93.7 | 186/0 | 1641 | 1641 | 3.0M | 77s | .047 | NO (-4.4)
topk5 | 90.3 | 94.8 | 194/0 | 2735 | 2680 | 4.9M | 118s | .043 | NO (-3.3)
topk10 | 92.9 | 97.8 | 197/0 | 5470 | 5470 | 10.0M | 229s | .042 | yes
combo 1024+topk10 | 93.7 | 97.8 | 214/0 | 5470 | 5470 | 15.5M | 244s | .045 | yes
combo 2048+topk10 | 96.3 | 98.5 | 225/0 | 5470 | 5470 | 25.0M | 289s | .053 | yes
L2 limits: state cap 32000 chars (HTTP 400 state_too_long, not 413); request cap 131072 input tokens, every question re-reads state; K=32 ok, K=40+ fails at 3k-char state.
L2 drift on 2228 real pairs: K=8 max .0085 mean 2e-4 (0 over .01); K=16 max .0092 (0 over); K=4 max .0109 (1 over, borderline). K=8: 5.7x fewer req, 2.9x less wall, 2.4x fewer chars.
3-note projection, validated: baseline model vs replay actual 4674/4434, 5973/5853, 6881/6881 (cap 120/unit binds uncited units, compressing L1 doc-mode gains).
note | replay judg/wall | combo2048+topk10 judg/req/reqB8/wall | combo1024+topk10
iter-04 (45u) | 4434/188s | 2100/2100/263/111s | 2100/2100/263/94s
iter-12 (60u) | 5853/251s | 2500/2500/313/132s | 2500/2500/313/112s
iter-18 (68u) | 6881/285s | 2980/2980/373/157s | 2980/2980/373/133s
Recommend 2048 chunks + top-10 filter + batch-8: benchmark 6.7x fewer judgments, 13x faster wall (unbatched pattern), 53x fewer requests batched; doc-mode ~2.3x fewer judgments, ~19x fewer requests; recall UP (+3.0/+0.4) with 0 false at 0.99.
Risks: bigger chunks dilute short evidence (not seen here: 48 arxiv papers); topk10 misses 1 positive vs exhaustive at bar (197 vs 198); batching reuses one state read, a server-side scoring change would need re-proof; per-call cap 120 still truncates uncited units at 1024.
Adopting 1024/2048 chunks changes the splitter output: bump SECTION_CHUNKING_VERSION (src/core/verify/store.ts), add property/golden tests, re-pin models.lock.json digests only if changed (rerun parity gate); old registries stay readable, new chunks get new revisions. L2/L3 need no bump (no chunk change). Raw: docs/benchmarks/verify-speed-study-2026-10-15.json.
